decisions.reason: The Lax clause used eigenvalues at arbitrary states in G although its supplier defines ordered real eigenvalues only on N. For f(x,y)=(y,x^2/2), Df has eigenvalues +/-sqrt(x) on x>0 but no real eigenvalues on x<0. The repaired clause requires both states in the stated hyperbolicity set N; the Rankine-Hugoniot identity remains valid on all of G.

F3 attributed weak-solution necessity to a definition that only names the algebraic RH identity. F4 already supplies the complete moving-jump equivalence and initial trace, so this is a nonfatal citation defect. F3 now states exactly the definition. The Roe scalar (uL+uR)/2 has all required properties, and the stationary (-1,1) jump has entropy production 2/3>0 for eta=u^2/2 and q=u^3/3.

The intended threshold is correct, but the ordered phrase left velocity then right velocity followed by their difference makes the signed gap ambiguous/reversed. Explicitly vR-vL=uR-uL-2(cL+cR)/(gamma-1)=Phi(0+). F3 now cites only the actual positive-pressure velocity/contact interface, and step 4.1 derives its limiting velocities from step 2.1. Both derivative formulas are positive, match at pK, and the explicit P gives Phi(P)>0; IVT and strict increase prove the unchanged existence/uniqueness statement.

The separate result exists: lem-euler-pressure-solver-bracket-and-termination is placed immediately after the intervening mixed-curve lemma on the same A page and depends on this algorithm. Its induction proves root containment and width <=(3/4)^k P, and its proof checks the finite one-update Newton call against the actual published procedures. The algorithm supplies the operational definition; adding the property lemma to deps would create a cycle. No missing guarantee or repair is established.

The original coefficient calculation was correct for r-=(1,-1), r+=(1,1), but its strength bound did not bind the solver radii to that normalization. The example now selects those constant fields before delta and eta, cites the integral/mixed-curve definitions, and solves their IVPs to obtain Psi(U,sigma)=U+sigma*r. Consequently sigma-=sigma+=-epsilon/2 is in the strength box, uniqueness identifies the composition, and direct multiplication verifies the two ordered contact jump balances.

The geometric budget inequality is sufficient, not necessary. The algorithm may return early at an exact Newton root or when an actual bracket is narrow enough even if the worst-case bound fails. Step 3.1 now states this explicitly and makes root containment conditional on the actual budget-exhausted status. The Sod pressure signs, positive-density state conversion, sound speeds and contact matching remain correct: Phi(0+)<0 and Phi(1/10)<0<Phi(1), hence 1/10<p*<1.

The actual local solver proof 2.1 explicitly observes that zero strengths solve the equal-data composition equation and invokes local uniqueness; its mixed-curve and rarefaction definitions have Psi_i(0;u)=u. The theorem constructs only the ordered elementary waves, so zero strengths give the constant profile. Thus F2 is an established consequence of the cited supplier, not an assertion of uniqueness among all weak solutions. Evaluating the physical flux gives G(u,u)=f(u), and each oriented interface flux cancels in the finite cyclic sum, including n=1. No repair is needed.

interface_changes.comparison: Direct literal comparison of the originally read Definition and current Definition; only the Lax hyperbolicity-domain clause changed.
interface_changes.before:
For a system as in [[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], a
discontinuity with constant states $u_L,u_R\in G$ and speed $s\in\mathbb R$ is
a **Rankine–Hugoniot jump** if
$$f(u_R)-f(u_L)=s(u_R-u_L).$$
For a strictly hyperbolic system and $1\le i\le m$, it is a **strict Lax
$i$-shock** if it is a Rankine–Hugoniot jump and
$$\lambda_j(u_L)<s\ (j<i),\qquad \lambda_i(u_R)<s<\lambda_i(u_L),\qquad s<\lambda_j(u_R)\ (j>i).$$
An empty family of inequalities is omitted. A linearly-degenerate contact has
equal $i$-speeds on both sides, so it is not a strict Lax shock.
interface_changes.after:
For a system as in [[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]], a
discontinuity with constant states $u_L,u_R\in G$ and speed $s\in\mathbb R$ is
a **Rankine–Hugoniot jump** if
$$f(u_R)-f(u_L)=s(u_R-u_L).$$
For a system strictly hyperbolic on $N\subseteq G$, states $u_L,u_R\in N$,
and $1\le i\le m$, it is a **strict Lax $i$-shock** if it is a Rankine–Hugoniot jump and
$$\lambda_j(u_L)<s\ (j<i),\qquad \lambda_i(u_R)<s<\lambda_i(u_L),\qquad s<\lambda_j(u_R)\ (j>i).$$
An empty family of inequalities is omitted. A linearly-degenerate contact has
equal $i$-speeds on both sides, so it is not a strict Lax shock.
